brief: Markets start the week firm. Trump talked up escalation with Iran over the weekend but took no military action, and diplomatic channels stay open. Bessent/He groundwork ahead of Thursday's Trump-Xi meeting raises hope of bridging a trade deal, though the author calls it far from certain. Energy sees no fresh disruption: crude is lower and Saudi exports are recovering despite the East-West pipeline still being impaired, with some hope of SPR releases. Rates and rate vol are the biggest macro risk: Friday broke the usual energy-rates correlation, with WTI down about 1.6% even as 2-year yields sold to about 4.74% and 10-year yields pushed through 5%, and the MOVE index rebid to 80.6. The author calls a rates-energy disanchoring premature and views rates as following energy. Positioning already covered last week per Prime and CFTC data despite horrendous breadth, read as a coiled spring for a violent short-covering snapback, hedged via Russell calls. The AI dip is a buying opportunity given an unchanged product cycle. Meta's Muse app reached No. 1 on the US Apple App Store within a week, prompting a call to watch the CPU/cloud compute trade, not just GPUs. German election results risk policy gridlock rather than reform.
